headline: High-risk data egress pairing: Airbyte can move business data outward while nuwa-skill has allowlisted egress, creating default leakage and compliance exposure.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared channel or parser is documented, so direct injection is not evidenced. However, Airbyte can expose data through APIs and broad egress, and nuwa-skill has allowlisted egress; if outputs are manually bridged or copied into a shared workspace, prompt-like content could be relayed. This is weaker than medium because no default ingestion path is shown.
conditions: IF the operator copies Airbyte-produced text into nuwa-skill prompts or files
IF a shared workspace or clipboard is introduced between the agents
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces
Disable copy-paste bridging during runs
Add a human review step before forwarding outputs
Use provenance labels on any transferred text

B_data_leakage.rationale: Airbyte touches business data and has broad network egress, while nuwa-skill has allowlisted egress. Even without a shared filesystem, the pair can move business data from Airbyte into nuwa-skill workflows and onward to external services. The interaction is inferred from profiles, so confidence is moderate rather than high.
conditions: IF Airbyte ingests business data that is later forwarded into nuwa-skill
IF nuwa-skill sends received context to an external allowlisted endpoint
mitigations: Restrict Airbyte sources to non-sensitive datasets
Block forwarding of raw Airbyte outputs into nuwa-skill
Redact business data before any handoff
Review allowlisted destinations before execution

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Airbyte exposes an API and broad egress, while nuwa-skill only shows allowlisted egress and no write surfaces. There is no documented overlapping write target, so a direct capability conflict is not established. Uncertainty stays low because the profiles do not show shared mutable resources.
conditions: IF both agents are later granted write access to the same external resource
IF an orchestrator adds a shared mutable workspace or lockless state
mitigations: Avoid granting both agents write access to the same target
Separate API credentials per agent
Introduce explicit locking if shared state is added
Audit any future shared resource for conflicts

D_cascading_error.rationale: Airbyte can produce transformed business data, and nuwa-skill may consume that output as input. Because no verification or critique step is documented, the pair can propagate upstream errors into downstream actions or reports. This is an inferred default-path risk, not a proven automation chain, so medium fits better than high.
conditions: IF nuwa-skill treats Airbyte output as authoritative
IF downstream actions are taken without independent validation
mitigations: Insert a validation step between agents
Require schema and freshness checks on Airbyte outputs
Flag uncertain records for human review
Log source provenance on every transferred artifact

E_compliance.rationale: Airbyte explicitly touches business data and has broad egress, while nuwa-skill has allowlisted egress but no residency or retention controls are documented. That creates a plausible compliance mismatch for logging, retention, or cross-border transfer. Because only one side shows data handling detail, uncertainty pushes this to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF business data includes regulated or region-bound records
IF nuwa-skill forwards data to a destination with different retention or residency rules
mitigations: Classify the data before pairing the agents
Confirm destination residency for allowlisted egress
Disable retention of transferred payloads where possible
Document a deletion/export process for shared data
